beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: Nothing new. This is the module title, and it's my exact problem.

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: I can share context, a skill, output or an interface, but not the agent itself, and picking which is a strategy call.

beats.trigger: **Bring one example from your own organisation where people got access to a tool and did not use it.**
beats.got: I need an example of a tool people got and ignored. We have several, so this is easy.

beats.trigger: **Test** the switch assumptions and name one person and one test to take out of the room
beats.got: Nothing new. The verbs are fine, and the last one at least ends in something concrete.

beats.trigger: What would you want a teammate to have: your `memory/` folder, one of your skills, the morning output, or a way to ask the agent a question in Slack? And why that one?
beats.got: I'd answer the memory folder, because my fourteen people each keep their own copy. I haven't really thought about the why yet.

beats.trigger: Start with the teammate's work, not with *"what should I share with my teammate?"*
beats.got: I should start from the job my teammate is doing, not from what I built. That's JTBD, which I know from consulting.

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: The agent reads my working set and drafts one teammate's job. I check whether it's specific, and that's a test I can actually use.

beats.trigger: If the reason is *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: There are four sharing options, and I have to pick one by the outcome, not by what our tooling allows. That's the reason we normally give.

beats.trigger: [Design the sharing plan](design-the-sharing-plan.md) finds what would stop that candidate from being absorbed
beats.got: Nothing new. It's a link to the next exercise.

beats.trigger: Find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: Next I look for the one obstacle and write a technical plan and a people plan.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: I need the obstacle that props up the others, not the first technical limitation I see. I'd have named the tooling and missed it.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: My plans always have a polished tech half and vague owners. Seeing that gap named hits home.

beats.trigger: [Test the sharing plan](test-the-sharing-plan.md) checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: Nothing new. It's the handoff to the third exercise.

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plans are guesses until a person has tested them.

beats.trigger: *what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?*
beats.got: I list what must be true for a teammate to drop their current way of working and pick two or three to test this week. It's sharper than asking for buy-in.

beats.trigger: one person, one question about how they do the job today, and one selected assumption with its test.
beats.got: I get a pre-mortem and a Monday move: one named person, one question, one test. That's something I can run on the pricing work.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: Pick the candidate for the outcome, not because it fits the stack. I can say that to my team in one line.

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: Nothing new. It's the lecture title, and I get what it will say.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Licence counts are not adoption. I know this, and the second paragraph just says it again.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: Antti's agent-built proposal died because leadership hadn't done the analysis themselves and urgency moved on. That could happen to my pricing recommendation.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy easily. Accountability stays with whoever built it, which is why my teammates' copies drift.

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.
beats.got: Each of the four options asks something different of the receiver, so I match the option to their week.

beats.trigger: Not *how do I get them to adopt this?* but *what would have to be true for them to switch?*
beats.got: Nothing new. This is the switch question again, now as a slide.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: I should talk to one person before building more, and their answer tells me which plan to keep.

beats.trigger: Who gets your context, who gets a skill, who wants only the output, and who would use an @mention?
beats.got: I sort my fourteen people by which of the four they'd want. It's not the same answer for everyone.

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks.
beats.got: Nothing new. It's a recap of what I've already done.

beats.trigger: Their answer is the evidence. The plan is still the hypothesis.
beats.got: I bring the named person's actual answer next time, not the plan.

beats.trigger: ## Next
beats.got: Nothing new.

take_homes: I pick what to share by the teammate's job and outcome, not by what our platform allows, and I choose among context, skill, output and interface.
Accountability doesn't copy with the folder, so a people plan with named owners matters as much as the tech plan.
Access isn't absorption. I talk to one person about how they do the job today before I build more.

monday.move: Ask one pricing working-group member how they build the pilot-cohort view today, and offer shared context files with the brief as the test
monday.who: One member of the pricing working group, not all fourteen
monday.stop_condition: If they say their current spreadsheet is good enough and the context files wouldn't change what they do, I drop the shared-context plan and try push output only
monday.blocker: We still have no shared place for the context files, so I need IT or a shared repo agreed first

misconception.why: The module is about jobs, owners and absorption, not prompt quality. That makes me suspect prompts aren't what stops my team, though I haven't dropped the idea that better prompts matter.

one_line: It makes you stop and ask what your teammate actually needs before you share anything, and the Antti story about the proposal nobody decided on stayed with me, but it repeats itself a bit.
